question.text:
Consider the following grammar where uppercase letters are non-terminals and lowercase/symbols are terminals:

  • $E \rightarrow E \uparrow T \mid T$
     
  • $T \rightarrow f \cdot T \mid f$
     
  • $A \rightarrow g \mid \epsilon$
     
  • $B \rightarrow g \mid \epsilon$
     
  • $S \rightarrow A c \mid B d$
     

Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding this grammar?

  1. THE OPERATOR ' $\uparrow$ ' IS RIGHT ASSOCIATIVE WHILE '$\cdot$' IS LEFT ASSOCIATIVE.
     
  2. THE GRAMMAR IS $\operatorname{LL}(1)$ BECAUSE IT CONTAINS NO EPSILON PRODUCTIONS FOR THE TOP-LEVEL SYMBOL $E$.
     
  3. THE OPERATOR ' $\uparrow$ ' IS LEFT ASSOCIATIVE WHILE '$?$' IS RIGHT ASSOCIATIVE.
     
  4. THE GRAMMAR IS NOT $\operatorname{LL}(1)$ .

question.text:
Consider the following grammar rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}
& S \rightarrow A b \mid B a \\
& A \rightarrow d \mid \epsilon \\
& B \rightarrow d \mid \epsilon
\end{aligned}
$$


Why is this grammar NOT $\mathrm{LL}(1)$?

  1. The grammar is $\mathrm{LL}(1)$ because it is in Greibach Normal Form
     
  2. The grammar is $\mathrm{LL}(1)$ because it is not left-recursive
     
  3. The grammar is $\mathrm{LL}(1)$ because $\operatorname{FIRST}(A) \cap \operatorname{FIRST}(B)=\emptyset$
     
  4. The grammar is not $\mathrm{LL}(1)$
